title: CodeBurn — Task-Level Token Cost Analytics TUI
description: CodeBurn (getagentseal/codeburn) is an interactive TUI dashboard that reads Claude Code's local JSONL session transcripts (~/.claude/projects/) and classifies every interaction into 13 deterministic categories based on tool usage patterns — no additional LLM calls required. Shows token and cost breakdown by task type, tool, model, MCP server, and project. Also tracks one-shot success rate per activity type. Cross-platform: supports Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Pi, and GitHub Copilot. Install: npm install -g codeburn. Fills a genuine gap — ccusage provides cost-per-day, but not cost-per-task-type or which activity categories are most expensive. Featured on Hacker News Show HN with positive reception. Validated via awesome-claude-code issue #1550.
relevance: MEDIUM — fills observability gap. Complementary to ccusage (date-level) with task-type granularity. No registry equivalent.

evaluation.reasoning: Novel cost observability tool with genuine gap fill (capability_expansion=70): ccusage shows cost-per-day; CodeBurn shows cost-per-task-type (13 deterministic categories) and one-shot success rate per activity. No equivalent in registry. Integration (100): npm install -g codeburn, zero configuration. Token efficiency (50): observability tool — doesn't affect session token usage, helps identify wasteful patterns externally. Maintenance (70): cross-platform, npm-distributed, Show HN validated, awesome-claude-code listed. Community validation (70): Show HN positive reception + awesome-claude-code issue #1550 — solid 100-1k range signal. Integration action: document install in registry, note as complement to ccusage for task-level cost analysis.
